HL4W NixOS Installation Guide

A modern configuration repo built on NixOS 26.05 + Home Manager
Hyprland · Niri · DMS Shell · Noctalia Shell · Fcitx5 + RIME

Requirements

💾
Disk space
At least 20 GiB; 40+ GiB recommended (the Nix store keeps growing)
🌐
Internet
Required — the installer downloads packages; use Chinese mirrors for faster downloads
🖥️
GPU
NVIDIA / AMD / Intel all supported; Hyprland auto-selects the right driver
📡
UEFI boot
Legacy BIOS not supported — enable UEFI mode in your BIOS
NixOS ISO

Download the latest Stable ISO (26.05) from nixos.org/download, flash it to a USB drive and boot the target machine.

Pick your path

Choose based on your current state:

  • Option 1 · Fresh machine booted from the NixOS ISO — one-script partitioning, encryption, and deploy
  • Option 2 · Machine already running NixOS — generate host config and nixos-rebuild
  • Option 3 · Full manual control over every step

Option 1: Fresh install (booted from NixOS ISO)

The most hands-off option. setup-disk.sh handles everything from partitioning to hardware config — you only run nixos-install at the end.

Data warning

This script will wipe the target disk and create a GPT partition table. Double-check the device path and back up any important data before running.

Disk layout (auto-created)

p1  EFI 512MiB          # systemd-boot
p2  Data partition       # LUKS2 container (encrypted) or LVM PV (plain)
    └─ VG vg
        ├─ swap LV      # 10% of disk, clamped 2–16 GiB
        └─ root LV      # fills the rest → /mnt
/home lives under / — no separate partition
1
Boot into the installer, download the script

After booting the ISO, log into the terminal (root by default) and run:

curl -fsSL -o setup-disk.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl4w/nixfiles/master/scripts/setup-disk.sh
chmod +x setup-disk.sh
2
Run setup-disk.sh

The script partitions the disk, creates LUKS2+LVM, formats, mounts, clones the repo to /mnt/etc/nixos, and invokes install.sh to generate host config and hardware config.

# Basic usage (interactive prompts for components; Enter keeps defaults)
sudo ./setup-disk.sh /dev/nvme0n1 my-hostname myuser

# Or specify everything in one shot
sudo ./setup-disk.sh -T desktop -W hyprland -S dms /dev/nvme0n1 my-hostname myuser

# To skip disk encryption (not recommended), add -c
sudo ./setup-disk.sh -c /dev/nvme0n1 my-hostname myuser

Flags

FlagDescriptionValues / default
-THost typedesktop (default) / laptop / server
-WWindow managerhyprland (default) / niri; skipped on server
-SDesktop shelldms (default) / noctalia; skipped on server
-cSkip disk encryptionboolean; encrypted by default
-yNon-interactive modeauto-confirms all prompts; for CI / automation
3
Review hardware config, install the system

When the script finishes, the repo is at /mnt/etc/nixos. If this is your first run with a specific substituter you may want to run nix flake update. Then install:

cd /mnt/etc/nixos
# Optional: update flake inputs (recommended after a fresh clone from a new mirror)
nix flake update
# Install
sudo nixos-install --flake .#my-hostname
4
Reboot into your new system 
reboot

After reboot, log in with the user account you configured. The SDDM display manager starts automatically — pick the Hyprland or Niri session.

Option 2: Existing NixOS system, host config only

1
Clone the repo 
git clone https://github.com/hl4w/nixfiles.git
cd nixfiles

# Generate flake.lock before the first run (pins deps, incl. oh-my-rime)
nix flake update
2
Run install.sh

Interactive mode asks in sequence: hostname, username, Git info, host type, window manager, desktop shell, polkit agent.

chmod +x scripts/install.sh
./scripts/install.sh

# Or all flags at once (non-interactive)
# ./scripts/install.sh -y -U myuser -H my-hostname -T desktop -W hyprland -S dms -P kde
3
Verify hardware config and deploy 
# install.sh auto-runs nixos-generate-config; confirm the file exists
ls hosts/my-hostname/hardware-configuration.nix || \
  sudo nixos-generate-config --show-hardware-config > hosts/my-hostname/hardware-configuration.nix

# Deploy system config (first build is slow — expect 10–30 min)
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#my-hostname

# Deploy user config
home-manager switch --flake .#myuser@my-hostname

Option 3: Manual deployment

For full control or when scripts don't apply to your scenario.

1
Clone + generate flake.lock 
git clone https://github.com/hl4w/nixfiles.git && cd nixfiles
nix flake update
2
Copy host template, generate hardware config 
cp -r templates/host-template hosts/my-hostname
# Add --root /mnt when inside the installer (target root mounted at /mnt)
nixos-generate-config --show-hardware-config > hosts/my-hostname/hardware-configuration.nix
3
Edit flake.nix to add the host + create the Home Manager user file

Inside the nixosConfigurations block of flake.nix, add:

"my-hostname" = mkHost "my-hostname";
touch home/hosts/my-hostname.nix
4
Build and deploy 
# Test build (no deploy)
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.my-hostname.config.system.build.toplevel

# Deploy system
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#my-hostname

# Deploy user config
home-manager switch --flake .#myuser@my-hostname

Build & verify

Fast syntax check (no compile)

nix flake check --no-build

Full test build

nix build .#nixosConfigurations.<hostname>.config.system.build.toplevel

Preview what would change

nixos-rebuild dry-activate --flake .#<hostname>

Rollback

# List generations
sudo nixos-rebuild list-generations

# Rollback to previous
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --rollback

# Rollback to a specific generation
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --generation <number>

# Home Manager rollback
home-manager rollback

Post-install config

Switch Catppuccin flavor

Edit the Theme value in classicui.conf inside home/common/input.nix — format catppuccin-{latte|frappe|macchiato|mocha}-{accent}. Then restart fcitx5 with fcitx5 -r.

Host-specific config options

Edit hosts/<hostname>/configuration.nix:

desktop.unified-theme = { themeMode = "auto"; dayStart = 6; nightStart = 18; };
desktop.shell = "dms";                  // dms / noctalia
desktop.windowManager = "hyprland";     // hyprland / niri
desktop.hostType = "desktop";           // desktop / laptop / server
desktop.polkitAgent = "kde";             // kde / hyprland

Add fonts

Append font packages to the fonts.packages list in modules/system/fonts.nix, then run sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<hostname>.

Updating

# After modifying system modules
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<hostname>

# After modifying user modules
home-manager switch --flake .#<username>@<hostname>

# Update flake inputs (nixpkgs, home-manager, etc.)
nix flake update

# One-shot flake update + rebuild
./scripts/update.sh

# Clean old generations + unreferenced store paths
./scripts/clean.sh -a

FAQ

How do I find the disk device?

In the ISO terminal run lsblk -d — find the device whose SIZE matches your disk (e.g. /dev/nvme0n1 for NVMe SSDs, /dev/sda for SATA SSDs/HDDs). The script derives partition names automatically (NVMe → p1/p2, SCSI → 1/2).

setup-disk.sh failed halfway — what now?

The script is idempotent only to the extent that it bails out if it detects existing partitions. Wipe the disk with wipefs -a /dev/xxx and re-run, or finish the remaining steps manually.

How do I regenerate flake.lock?

nix flake update updates everything; nix flake update nixpkgs updates a single input. Required after any change to the inputs block in flake.nix.

Hyprland / Niri won't start?

Ensure SDDM runs in Wayland mode and graphics drivers are installed. Hyprland 0.55+ requires configType = "hyprlang" (already set in the config). Check logs at ~/.local/share/hyprland/ or run hyprctl config -h to validate.

Fcitx5 won't switch to Chinese input?

Verify fcitx5 -d is running; check that $GTK_IM_MODULE / $QT_IM_MODULE equal fcitx (SDDM sets them automatically). Run fcitx5-diagnose for diagnostics.

Build is slow?

Non-Chinese users: make sure flake.nix and modules/system/default.nix mirror config points to mirrors.ustc.edu.cn and mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn. First build downloads everything; subsequent builds hit the binary cache automatically.
